name: Gaze+Hold
summary: With eyes only, the user closes one eye to grab what they are looking at, moves it by looking with the other eye, and opens the eye to let go.
howItWorks: The two eyes are used as separate inputs: closing one eye acts like holding down a mouse button on the gazed object, the open eye's gaze then provides continuous input (dragging, scrolling, panning, zooming, drawing a selection), and opening the closed eye ends the action. Because pointing alone never triggers anything, it avoids the Midas touch problem without dwell. Evaluated on a desktop (N=12, Tobii EyeX under a 27" monitor) with a drag-and-drop task; users were effective, and using the dominant or non-dominant eye made no difference to performance, usability or workload.
